The macOS app is signed and notarized, Settings has an About page, and Ond can stream as Opus.

### Downloads

| File | For |
| --- | --- |
| `Ond-0.4.3-macos-universal.dmg` (or `.zip`) | macOS 11 or later, Apple silicon and Intel |
| `Ond-0.4.3-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | Linux on x86_64, glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40, Debian 13) |
| `Ond-0.4.3-linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | Linux on ARM64, same requirements |
| `Ond-0.4.3-windows-x86_64.zip` | Windows 10 and 11. Still untested on real hardware; issues welcome. |

On NixOS or with Nix: `nix profile install github:Solidsilver/ond/v0.4.3`. Install steps for every platform are in the [README](https://github.com/Solidsilver/ond#install).

### Signed for macOS

- Ond is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so it opens on the first try. No more Open Anyway.
- The first time you open it after updating, macOS asks whether Ond may use its saved password. Choose Always Allow. It asks once because the app's signature changed.

### About and updates

- Settings › About shows the version and has Check for updates, with Check Now and when Ond last looked.
- When a new version is out, About shows its release notes, with Download and Skip.
- The update notice in the sidebar opens About. In the narrow window's icon rail, the gear has a dot.

### Opus streaming

- Settings › Playback › Streaming can convert to Opus, beside AAC and MP3. At the same bitrate Opus sounds better, which helps on mobile data. Your server needs an Opus transcoding; Navidrome has one unless it was removed.
